After the prisoners were taken away, Jabba also sentenced Porcellus to death since Oola and Jubnuk had both perished after eating his food, thus causing Jabba to believe that the chef had, in fact, hexed his food. Later, as Jabba boarded his private [[Sail barge/Legends|sail barge]], [[Khetanna/Legends|''Khetanna'']], he was approached by his head of security and only friend, [[Ephant Mon/Legends|Ephant Mon]], who had just spoken to Skywalker in the dungeons. Having sensed the Force in Luke, Mon tried to convince Jabba to free him. But because Jabba refused to listen, Mon decided not to accompany him to Carkoon, and the two ended their friendship. While Jabba and his entourage travelled aboard the ''Khetanna,'' the prisoners were carried to their doom on a smaller [[Skiff/Legends|skiff]]. On the way, Leia attempted to watch her friends from a window, but Jabba eventually forced her to return to him on this throne. The crime lord boasted that she would soon learn to appreciate him and made her drink from his goblet.[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' novelization]] Later, once they reached the pit, Jabba offered the prisoners a chance to beg for mercy. Luke warned Jabba once more, but the Hutt ignored the offer and ordered them to be thrown in. Just as Luke was to be thrown to the sarlacc, R2-D2, who was working on the sail barge at that time, launched Luke's [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] from a hidden compartment in his dome. Luke immediately launched an [[Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon|attack]] against the skiff guards, causing a state of panic to break out onboard ''Khetanna''. Amid the chaos, Leia shorted the lighting system, distracting Jabba. During the distraction, Leia jumped over Jabba's tail, wrapped her chain around the crime lord, and began strangling him. As a last act of desperation, Jabba activated Ree-Yees's hypnotic trigger in an effort to get him to grab Leia and self-destruct. Before Ree-Yees could do so, Jabba died. After being freed from her restraints by R2-D2, Leia and Luke met on the top deck of the sail barge. Luke had Leia point the deck gun into the bowels of the ship and set it off. Escaping to one of the skiffs, the successful rebels sped away from the exploding sail barge, which had become a funeral pyre for the once-great Jabba the Hutt. ===Aftermath (4 ABY—)=== Following the Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon, Dengar witnessed a Hutt transport land near the ''Khetanna'' debris field to recover what was left of Jabba's body.''[[The Mandalorian Armor]]'' Immediately following Jabba's demise, fighting broke out between the remnants of his criminal empire. Two small time criminals named [[Qes Dollis]] and [[Kisa Shaki]] tried to take over the Mos Eisley portion of his smuggling business, sparking a gang war. Meanwhile, a group of four [[Battle droid/Legends|war droids]] called the [[Mos Eisley Mourners]] were activated within a week and attempted to wipe out anyone that they identified as a possible responsible party.''[[Secrets of Tatooine]]'' [[File:Jabbabody.png|thumb|left|250px|Jabba's corpse, after his strangulation.]]The death of Jabba canceled the debts of many individuals, because of which Luke was held with considerable favor for removing that dangerous complication in people's lives. In response to his son's death, Zorba (fresh out of galactic prison) placed a bounty on Leia, which the Desilijic kajidic later extended to Han, Chewbacca, and Luke. The bounty was not formally rescinded until Leia's election as [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chief of State]], since the Hutts did not wish to further antagonize the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. Because of Luke's involvement in Jabba's death, [[Ka'Pa]], if not all the Hutts, grew distrustful to the [[New Jedi Order|Jedi]], which caused negotiations with Mara Jade on behalf of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] to be a bit shaky.''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Mysteries of the Sith]]'' [[Gorga Desilijic Aarrpo/Legends|Gorga]] the Hutt, Jabba's nephew, went to Jabba's palace seeking a part in his uncle's will. Gorga was given a small statue of a Hutt; a statue that held the key to Jabba's prized treasure trove. Gorga also desired the funeral urns of Jabba, but he had some competition: [[Spiker]] (who had somehow survived his encounter with Solo and Fett) and Big Gizz (who was found to have survived his encounter with [[Wrenga Jixton|Jix]] and Luke Skywalker). Upon learning of their boss's death, the happily reunited swooper duo sought out the deceased Hutt's legendary treasures, joined by Jabba's former servant, [[Onoh]]."[[The Jabba Tape]]" When the trio discovered the vaults, however, they activated a security system that nearly killed them. It was a recording made by Jabba, who knew that Gizz was still alive and had predicted that he would try to steal his riches. In its self-destruction, the booby-trapped tape almost killed the bikers. Later, to Gorga's horror, Gizz and Spiker dropped Jabba's urns on Gorga and his henchmen. The urns, of course, were destroyed in the process. Many years after Jabba's death, many Hutts wished that he still lived, for if he had, the Hutts believed that they would have avoided the disastrous [[Darksaber (superweapon)|Darksaber]] project and their treacherous deal with the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]. However, Jabba's organization did unwittingly help the Darksaber project; by scouring the Hutt's palace on Tatooine, Durga's Besadii agents procured the access codes to the ex-Imperial databases on Coruscant, where they found the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] plans needed to assemble their own superweapon. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|Soon you will learn to appreciate me.|Jabba, to [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]|translated=1|}} [[File:JabbaDesilijicTattoo.jpg|thumb|175px|Jabba had his [[Desilijic/Legends|Desilijic]] [[Kajidic/Legends|kajidic]] symbol [[Tattoo/Legends|tattooed]] on his right arm.]] Jabba, a typical Hutt, was greedy, malicious, pragmatic, and adept at bending others to his will. He was also prideful, and he collected things like trophies and trinkets as reminders of his power. He also enjoyed cruelty, in the form of [[Torture/Legends|torture]], executions, and subjugation (as with the case of his palace). He did this for enjoyment, as well as for practical purposes of logistics and need. He kept the oddity [[Salacious B. Crumb/Legends|Salacious B. Crumb]] simply because he was as humorous to him as he was annoying to others. He also had a lust for female humanoids, often enslaving them for his pleasure, including [[Oola/Legends|Oola]], and Princess [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]. His humanoid female fetish was also implied by close Hutt associates of Jabba to not be a typical Hutt trait.[[The Han Solo Trilogy (hardcover)|''The Han Solo Trilogy'' hardcover]] However, this trait turned out to be his downfall when Leia killed him. Despite his cruel, greedy and sadistic nature, Jabba had shown a softer side as evident when he was overjoyed at the return of his Huttlet, [[Rotta/Legends|Rotta]]. He was also furious and a little shocked at his uncle [[Ziro Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Ziro's]] hand in his son's kidnapping. These two attributes point to the possibility that Jabba cared about and respected family, to a certain extent. Likewise, he also seemed to contain some empathy to other people's love of their offspring, as evidenced by his ultimately allowing [[Notluwiski Papanoida/Legends|Notluwiski Papanoida]], who arrived to search for his daughters, to present evidence and arrest the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]] after Papanoida reminded him of his love for his own son. He also expressed regret when [[Ephant Mon/Legends|Ephant Mon]] implied that he thought his relationship with Jabba was based on a debt, not on friendship.{{StoryCite|story=Old Friends: Ephant Mon's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}} Jabba considered Han Solo his best smuggler, and had a measure of fondness for him, though he was frustrated that Han had once "dropped his cargo at the first sign of an Imperial starship" and placed a bounty on his head when Han was unable to pay Jabba the money he owed him. Jabba eventually grew tired of Han and, no longer concerned about Han's debt to him, kept his frozen state (brought to him by Boba Fett) as a wall decoration. When Han was freed from cryogenic freezing by Leia, Jabba had Han taken prisoner and later attempted to feed him, along with Luke Skywalker and Chewbacca, to the sarlacc. Jabba's right arm bore a [[Tattoo/Legends|tattoo]] of his [[Kajidic/Legends|kajidic]] clan, the [[Desilijic/Legends|Desilijic]]. While fighting [[Beldorion]] on [[Nam Chorios]], [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] remembered from her time in Jabba's palace that Jabba's fat hid a great deal more muscle than anyone suspected, and for all his apparent sluggishness, he could move deceptively fast across a room, particularly when his temper was roused.''[[Planet of Twilight]]'' ==Behind the scenes== ===Origins=== {{Quote|What's this ship coming to? We've got a good-for-nothing 'cabin boy' and a disintegrating science officer.|Jabba the Hutt comments on Han Solo and Captain [[Montross (bounty hunter)|Montross]] in the second draft of ''Star Wars''|}} Jabba Desilijic Tiure was created by [[George Lucas]], the creator of ''[[Star Wars]]'', but was known only as Jabba the Hutt until his identification as a member of the Desilijic Kajidic in later [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] works.''[[Galaxy Guide 11: Criminal Organizations]]'' Jabba the Hutt appears in Lucas's second draft of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']], [[1975]]'s ''[[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars]]'', as the larger and mangier slavering hulk of two gruff and grisly pirates. The pirates, along with Han Solo and Chewbacca, work for the pirate Captain [[Oxus]] aboard a [[TDF104]] starship.{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarz.com/starkiller/scripts/thestarwars_second_draft.htm|text=ADVENTURES OF THE STARKILLER (episode one) - "The Star Wars" by George Lucas|work=Starkiller - The Jedi Bendu Script Site|archivedate=20020809190949}} Lucas's third draft, entitled ''[[The Star Wars: From The Adventures of Luke Starkiller]]'', introduced Jabba as the leader of a band of pirates who had paid for Han Solo's ship. Still a gross and slavering hulk, Jabba approaches Solo in Mos Eisley and demands use of the ship, but is thwarted when the Corellian blasts away from [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]] with Luke, Kenobi, and the droids.{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarz.com/starkiller/scripts/thestarwars_third_draft.htm|text="THE STAR WARS" - From The Adventures of Luke Starkiller by George Lucas|work=Starkiller - The Jedi Bendu Script Site|archivedate=20100428061152}} A tweaked version of this latter scene went on to appear in the final script, and was filmed during production of the first ''Star Wars'' film. However, time and money constraints [[Content cut from Star Wars|prevented]] Lucas from including it in the film's final cut.''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] Featurette [[File:Declanjabba.jpg|thumb|left|225px|Declan Mulholland as Jabba the Hutt during filming of ''Star Wars'']] The final script of ''Star Wars'' changed the spelling of his name to "Jabba the Hut" and described him as a "fat, slug-like creature with eyes on extended feelers and a huge ugly mouth."{{DB|character|jabbathehutt|Jabba the Hutt}} Lucas intended for him to be a furry, Chewbacca-esque character, and had actor [[Declan Mulholland]] play the role wearing a shaggy coat. Mulholland would have been replaced with a stop-motion creature during post-production had the scene not ended up on the [[Content cut from Star Wars|cutting room floor]]. The scene did appear in the film's [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] and [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] [[Star Wars (1977) 2|adaptation]], however, both using the "Hut" spelling of the screenplay.[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novel]][[Star Wars (1977) 2|''Star Wars'' (1977) 2]] The film's [[1981]] [[Star Wars (radio)|radio drama]] replaced Jabba with his henchman [[Heater (henchman)|Heater]].[[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio drama]] [[File:JabbaHut.jpg|thumb|150px|"Jabba the Hut" (left) as he appeared in Marvel Comics' ''Star Wars'' series]] The novelization describes Jabba as a "great mobile tub of muscle and suet topped by a shaggy scarred skull," while in the comic issue [[Star Wars (1977) 2|''Star Wars'' (1977) 2]], Jabba appears as a member of a walrus-like species also present in the Mos Eisley Cantina, later identified as a [[Nimbanel/Legends|Nimbanel]].''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]'' This depiction of Jabba went on to appear in two additional issues of the [[Marvel Comics]]-[[Star Wars (1977)|issued]] ''Star Wars'' series.[[Star Wars (1977) 28|''Star Wars'' (1977) 28]][[Star Wars (1977) 37|''Star Wars'' (1977) 37]] Although no official [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]] has addressed this issue, [[Abel G. Peña]], a ''Star Wars'' author who has fit other continuity problems from the Marvel series into ''Star Wars'' [[canon]],{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/96/indexp2.html|series=Aliens in the Empire|text=Part 1: Hierarchy of Power}} has suggested that the discrepancy between Jabba's Nimbanel appearance and his canonical depiction as a slug-like creature can be explained by retconning "Jabba the Hut" into actually being [[Mosep Binneed/Legends|Mosep Binneed]], Jabba the Hutt's Nimbanel accountant.{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=239641&start=30|thread=Marvels take on Star wars|user=Jeff Ferguson|date=2006-01-28|time=8:58 PM|check=1}}{{JCFCite|url=posts/27823869|board=Literature|thread=Aliens of the Empire (Part 2 now up)|user=Halagad_Ventor|date=2007-12-05|time=1:33 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200801202545/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/aliens-of-the-empire-part-2-now-up.27707732/page-5}} Although not present in the final version of ''Star Wars'', Jabba is mentioned several times in the film as being owed a large sum of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] by Han Solo. In [[1980]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], Jabba again does not appear, but Solo's continued debt causes him to be frozen in carbonite and taken to the Hutt during the climax of the film. The official [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry claimed that the release of ''Empire'' solidified the spelling of "Hutt," with a double t, but in fact his name is still spelled with a single t in the ''Empire'' [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization]] and [[Star Wars (1977) 39|comic adaptation]]. It was not until the publication of material contemporaneous with ''Return of the Jedi'' in [[1983]] that the spelling was officially changed to "Hutt." But nothing specified, as of 1983, whether "Hutt" was a title, family name, species, or other identifier. Jabba was the only Hutt in canon, and was not necessarily considered typical of his species: the [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Return of the Jedi'' novelization]] stated that Jabba had once had hair, which he had lost to disease. Several years later, [[West End Games]] sourcebooks contradicted this by specifying that all Hutts shared Jabba's basic form, including hairlessness. They also established that "Hutt" was the name of Jabba's species.''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]'' ===A slug is born=== {{Quote|One advantage of puppets (as I mentioned when talking about live shows) comes from their ability to improvise, to change a performance (either because the director has a fresh idea, or because the actor changed their way of playing the scene). Our Jabba actually plays with the actors, he genuinely 'acts' on set, and had real presence (sometimes quite scary).|Toby Philpott|{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsinterviews1|url=2010/01/toby-philpott-interview.html|name=Star Wars Interviews|text=Toby Philpott interview - Jabba the Hutt - Star Wars}}}} Jabba the Hutt appeared and played a large role in [[Richard Marquand]]'s 1983 film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. Lucas wanted the character redesigned, and told [[Industrial Light & Magic]] visual effects supervisor [[Phil Tippett]] to design something alien, grotesque, and like the actor [[Wikipedia:Sydney Greenstreet|Sydney Greenstreet]]. Tippett settled on the idea of Jabba being a large, sluglike pulsating mass of flesh,''[[Empire of Dreams: The Story of the Star Wars Trilogy]]'' although the film's costume designer, [[Nilo Rodis-Jamero]], had conceived of him being a refined character similar to an older [[Wikipedia:Orson Welles|Orson Welles]].''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]'' One of Tippett's concept models of the character saw Jabba wear a [[Wikipedia:Fez (hat)|Fez hat]] in the style of Greenstreet. [[File:In_jabba.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A schematic showing the team of puppeteers that brought Jabba to life]] After constructing several models, Tippett turned work over to makeup supervisor [[Stuart Freeborn]], whose team built a one-ton puppet over the course of three months costing half a million dollars. During filming, the puppet was operated by a team of puppeteers.''[[From Star Wars to Jedi: The Making of a Saga]]'' One puppeteer stood behind Jabba and controlled his head; each of the Hutt's arms were controlled by someone sitting inside of the puppet; a small performer sat inside the puppet and controlled Jabba's tail; and his eyes were radio-controlled by a final operator. [[David Barclay]] was the chief puppeteer and controlled the right arm and mouth, [[Toby Philpott]] controlled the left arm and tongue, and [[Mike Edmonds]] was inside the tail.{{InsiderCite|67|Beyond the Valley of the Ewoks}} Sculptor [[John Coppinger]] has credited the team's performance as having allowed the other actors on set to react and relate to Jabba,{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsinterviews1|url=2010/01/john-coppinger-interview.html|name=Star Wars Interviews|text=John Coppinger interview - Jabba the Hutt - Star Wars}} and Philpott has praised the builders of the puppet for allowing the character to come alive. The interior body of the fifteen-foot-long puppet was made of fibreglass floating on springs that angled down from posts set onto an industrial turntable.{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/jedicouncil/interview/jcoppinger.shtml|text=Interview with John Coppinger - Animatronics Engineer for Return of the Jedi|work=[[TheForce.net]]|archivedate=20120907205246}} The puppeteers sat inside of the fibreglass shell, and airbags and latex skin were layered on its outside in order to fabricate the shape of Jabba's stomach. Philpott has described the interior as smelling like a fine collection of fumes of lubricants, paints, and glues. For several weeks, he and Barclay would spend most of a day inside the puppet, where they had access to a single headset and a monitor showing them a view of the puppet's exterior. On their request, Director Richard Marquand would speak and issue instructions directly to Jabba as if the Hutt were a real person. The exchanges helped them continuously practice controlling the puppet, and sustained the illusion of Jabba's reality for the other actors on set. The Jabba puppet was filmed on three different sets. On the sail barge set, the scene featuring his death originally called for [[Carrie Fisher]], the actress playing Princess Leia, to attack him from the front and kill him. His manner of death was changed to feature Leia attacking him from behind and choking him to death on the advice of George Lucas. Lucas was inspired by a scene depicting an obese character's death in the [[1972]] film [[Wikipedia:The Godfather|''The Godfather'']]. The puppet had to be repaired following each take of its death scene. Jabba's Huttese dialogue was recorded and spoken by [[Larry Ward]]. Sound effects accompanying movement of the puppet's limbs and mouth were created by a hand running through a bowl of cheese casserole and a muddy towel scraping along the inside of a garbage can.[[Ben Burtt]]'s commentary on the ''Return of the Jedi'' [[Star Wars home video releases#Star Wars Trilogy DVD set|DVD]] [[Jabba's theme|Jabba's Theme]], a musical leitmotif played on the [[Wikipedia:Tuba|tuba]], was often played during Jabba's screen time in ''Return of the Jedi''. ===From puppet to CGI=== {{Quote|I actually think it was a brave attempt, given the state of CGI then, but I believe they tried to do too much.|John Coppinger on the first CGI incarnation of Jabba the Hutt|}} [[File:Ataleoftwohutts.jpg|thumb|260px|Jabba as he appeared in the ''A New Hope'' 1997 Special Edition (top) and 2004 DVD Release (bottom).]] In [[1997]], Lucas re-released each entry of the [[Original trilogy]] as a [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] to commemorate the twentieth anniversary of the original film's release. His intent was to restore the deteriorating film negatives of the original movies while improving special effects and adding in scenes that hadn't previously been included. One such scene was Jabba's appearance in the original ''Star Wars'', as Lucas wanted to connect the film to ''Return of the Jedi''. Recent improvements in computer-generated imagery techniques allowed for Declan Mulholland to be replaced by a CGI Jabba. Visual effects supervisors working on the Special Edition created a CGI model of Jabba in a five-shot project that took one year to complete, but faced the problem of Han Solo's actor [[Harrison Ford]] having walked around Mulholland's back. On Lucas's advice, they edited the scene to make Solo step on Jabba's tail. The CGI Jabba was further polished and improved when the film was released on [[Star Wars home video releases#Star Wars Trilogy DVD set|DVD]] in [[2004]].{{WebCite|url=http://www.dvdactive.com/editorial/articles/star-wars-the-changes-part-one.html|text=Star Wars: The Changes|archivedate=20180708192254}} Jabba was given a cameo in the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. In the movie, he was again a CGI model, and was credited as playing "himself." His theme music can be heard briefly in the film, as well as in the DVD release of ''A New Hope''.''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' ([[Star Wars home video releases#Star Wars Trilogy DVD set|DVD]] release) ===In ''Star Wars'' media=== {{Quote|Kidnapped, Jabba the Hutt's son has been.|[[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] in the 2008 film ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''|}} In addition to appearing in three of the primary films of the ''Star Wars'' saga, Jabba has been featured in a wide variety of Expanded Universe works. The [[1996]] anthology of short stories ''[[Tales from Jabba's Palace]]'' explored the lives and backstories of the patrons of his court, revealing that many of them were plotting to kill him.''[[Tales from Jabba's Palace]]'' [[Dark Horse Comics]] released several one-shot Jabba comics in [[1995]] and 1996,''[[Star Wars: Jabba the Hutt]]'' and several reference books have expanded the character's backstory. The [[1991]] novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'' established that the smuggler [[Talon Karrde]] replaced Jabba at the top of the criminal underworld following the Hutt's death,''[[Heir to the Empire]]'' and a [[Adventures of a Jedi Prince|series]] of young-reader novels involved Jabba's father Zorba attempting to enact revenge on Princess Leia following the death of his son. Jabba played a large role in the [[2008]] film [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'']]. In the movie, following the kidnapping of the Hutt's son, Anakin Skywalker and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] embark on a quest to rescue the young Huttlet, hoping to gain the Republic access to hyperspace routes through Hutt Space during the Clone Wars. Jabba was voiced by [[Kevin Michael Richardson]]. [[Ed Asner]] provided vocal talents in the ''Return of the Jedi'' [[Return of the Jedi (radio)|radio drama]].[[Return of the Jedi (radio)|''Return of the Jedi'' radio drama]] [[Clint Bajakian]] voiced the Hutt in the video game [[Star Wars: Racer Revenge|''Racer Revenge'']].''[[Star Wars: Racer Revenge]]'' ===Impact on popular culture=== [[File:Pizzahutt.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Pizza the Hut]] In the years since the release of ''Return of the Jedi'', a wide variety of Jabba-related merchandise has been released, including scores of action figures,{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (toy line)|pack=Jabba the Hutt Action Playset|link=vintJabbaTheHutt.asp}}{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: The Power of the Force (1995 toy line)|pack=Jabba the Hutt and Han Solo|link=POTF2beasthan1.asp}}{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Episode I (toy line)|pack=Jabba the Hutt with 2-Headed Announcer|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/episodeIjabbaannouncer.asp}}{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|pack=Jabba the Hutt|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/sw04ultrajabba.asp}} busts,{{WebCite|url=http://www.comicstatues.com/statues-busts-props-item-746.html|text=Jabba The Hutt Statue GG|work=ComicStatues.com|nobackup=1}} and Halloween costumes.{{WebCite|url=http://old.boxwish.com/profiles/merchandise/fancy-dress/adult-jabba-the-hutt-inflatable-fancy-dress-costume|text=Adult Jabba the Hutt Inflatable Fancy Dress Costume|work=Boxwish|nobackup=1}} The character has been parodied many times, including on [[Wikipedia:South Park|South Park]].{{WebCite|url=http://www.southparkstudios.com/clips/151531/sally-struthers|text=Sally Struthers - Clips|work=South Park Studios|archivedate=20120527132530}} In literature and popular culture, Jabba's name and appearance have been used to represent obesity, corruption, greed, and anarchy. Authors [[Wikipedia:Marian Keyes|Marian Keyes]] and Laura Kalpakian have referenced the Hutt in their novels, respectively in regards to gluttony and a character's weight,{{BookCite|author=Marian Keyes|title=Under the Duvet: Shoes, Reviews, Having the Blues, Builders, Babies, Families and Other Calamities|publisher=HarperCollins|date=2001|isbn=0060562080}}{{BookCite|author=Laura Kalpakian|title=Steps and Exes: A Novel of Family|publisher=HarperCollins|date=2000|isbn=0380806592}} while comedian [[Wikipedia:Roseanne Barr|Roseanne Barr]] was frequently compared to Jabba by [[Wikipedia:The New York Observer|''The New York Observer'']] columnist Michael Thomas in what author W.C. Goodman called "vitriolic attacks based on her weight."{{BookCite|author=W. C. Goodman|title=The Invisible Woman: Confronting Weight Prejudice in America|publisher=Gürze Books|date=1995|isbn=0936077107}}. [[Wikipedia:Michael Jordan|Michael Jordan]] biographer Mitchell Krugel asserted that [[Wikipedia:Chicago Bulls|Chicago Bulls]] manager [[Wikipedia:Jerry Krause|Jerry Krause]] had a "Jabba the Hutt" image after making negative comments on Jordan's multi-million dollar contract.{{BookCite|author=Mitchell Krugel|title=One Last Shot: The Story of Michael Jordan's Comeback|publisher=St. Martin's Press|date=2003|isbn=0312992238}}. Further comparisons of the Hutt with greed, as well as anarchy, have been made by author [[Wikipedia:Koenraad Kuiper|Koenraad Kuiper]].{{BookCite|author=Koenraad Kuiper|container=Star Wars: An Imperial Myth|title=Journal of Popular Culture|number=21.4|date=1988}} In his book [[Wikipedia:The Dharma of Star Wars|''The Dharma of Star Wars'']], [[Wikipedia:Matthew Bortolin|Matthew Bortolin]] asserted that Jabba's way of life is contrary to the pursuit of the [[Wikipedia:Buddhism|Buddhist]] [[Wikipedia:Noble Eightfold Path|Noble Eightfold Path]].{{BookCite|author=Matthew Bortolin|title=The Dharma of Star Wars|publisher=Wisdom Publications|date=2005|isbn=0861714970}}. [[Wikipedia:California|California]] [[Wikipedia:Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] legislator [[Wikipedia:Jackie Goldberg|Jackie Goldberg]] has been caricatured as a grotesquely overweight Jabba the Hutt–like figure by the newspapers [[Wikipedia:Los Angeles Daily News|''Los Angeles Daily News'']] and [[Wikipedia:New Times LA|''New Times LA'']], the latter calling her "a human Jabba the Hutt who consumes the good while producing the bad."{{BookCite|author=Patrick Mallon|title=California Dictatorship|publisher=Xlibris|date=2004|isbn=1413467970}}. Finally, critic [[Wikipedia:William Ouchi|William Ouchi]] has accused American public school systems of being run by inefficient bureaucracy covered with Jabba-like layers of organizational fat.{{BookCite|author=William G. Ouchi|title=Making Schools Work: A Revolutionary Plan to Get Your Children the Education They Need|publisher=Simon and Schuster|date=2003|isbn=0743246306}}. ===Non-canon content=== [[File:JabbaVader.jpg|thumb|250px|Darth Vader confronts Jabba.]] In the alternate comic series ''[[Star Wars Infinities: The Empire Strikes Back]]'', Han Solo and Chewbacca arrive at Jabba's Palace to pay him, but are denied the opportunity by the Hutt and sentenced to die.
